claim: Lapatinib is an ATP-competitive inhibitor of HER2.
source: Here, we show that lapatinib, an ATP-competitive inhibitor of HER2, is able to induce proliferation cooperatively with the HER3 ligand neuregulin.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as a characterization of lapatinib.

claim: Lapatinib induces proliferation cooperatively with the HER3 ligand neuregulin.
source: Here, we show that lapatinib, an ATP-competitive inhibitor of HER2, is able to induce proliferation cooperatively with the HER3 ligand neuregulin.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data in Figure 1.

claim: The synergy between lapatinib and neuregulin depends on their ability to promote atypical HER2-HER3 heterodimerisation.
source: This counterintuitive synergy between inhibitor and growth factor depends on their ability to promote atypical HER2-HER3 heterodimerisation.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by FRET-FLIM data in Figure 3.

claim: Lapatinib stabilises a particular HER2 conformer.
source: By stabilising a particular HER2 conformer, lapatinib drives HER2-HER3 kinase domain heterocomplex formation.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by molecular modeling and FRET-FLIM experiments.

claim: The lapatinib-induced HER2-HER3 dimer exists in a head-to-head orientation distinct from the canonical asymmetric active dimer.
source: This dimer exists in a head-to-head orientation distinct from the canonical asymmetric active dimer.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by molecular modeling and mutational analysis in Figures 4-5.

claim: HER2 overexpression is an oncogenic driver in approximately 20% of all breast cancers.
source: Overexpression of HER2 is an oncogenic driver in approximately 20% of all breast cancers (Lovekin et al., 1991; Owens et al., 2004; Slamon et al., 1987).
evidence: This is stated with supporting citations from the literature.

claim: HER3 binds the growth factor neuregulin to induce heterodimerisation and signalling.
source: While HER2 itself has no known ligand, HER3 binds the growth factor neuregulin (NRG, also known as heregulin or HRG) to induce heterodimerisation and signalling (Sliwkowski et al., 1994).
evidence: This is stated with a supporting citation.

claim: HER3 has been implicated in therapeutic resistance to HER2-targeted therapy through a variety of mechanisms.
source: HER3 has been implicated in therapeutic resistance to HER2-targeted therapy through a variety of mechanisms, including receptor rephosphorylation, HER3 overexpression and increased NRG production (reviewed in [Claus et al., 2014]).
evidence: This is stated with a supporting citation to a review.

claim: In SKBR3, BT474, AU565, and HCC1419 cells treated with a range of lapatinib concentrations for 72 hr, the addition of 10 nM NRG rescues the drug-induced cytotoxicity except at very high drug concentrations.
source: In SKBR3, BT474, AU565, and HCC1419 cells treated with a range of lapatinib concentrations for 72 hr, the addition of 10 nM NRG rescues the drug-induced cytotoxicity except at very high drug concentrations (Figure 1a, Figure 1—figure supplement 1a–c).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by experimental data shown in the referenced figures.

claim: Low concentrations of lapatinib (~40–400 nM) are able to enhance proliferation in conjunction with 10 nM NRG by 25–30% compared to growth factor alone in SKBR3, BT474 and AU565 cell lines.
source: Interestingly, in the case of the SKBR3, BT474 and AU565 cell lines, low concentrations of lapatinib (~40–400 nM) are able to enhance proliferation in conjunction with 10 nM NRG by 25–30% compared to growth factor alone (Figure 1a, Figure 1—figure supplement 1a–b).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by experimental data shown in the referenced figures.

claim: Lapatinib does not strongly bind HER3 as compared to ATP and a panel of other inhibitors.
source: Using a thermal shift assay (TSA), which measures a shift in the thermal stability of a protein after ligand/inhibitor binding in vitro, we also show that lapatinib does not strongly bind HER3 as compared to ATP and a panel of other inhibitors (Figure 2a, see further below).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by TSA data shown in Figure 2a.

claim: Neratinib-NRG co-treatment did not show the synergistic proliferative phenotype observed with lapatinib-NRG.
source: Neratinib-NRG co-treatment did not show the synergistic proliferative phenotype observed with lapatinib-NRG, in either a cell counting assay, or in 3D spheroid formation (Figure 1—figure supplement 2a–d).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by experimental data shown in the referenced figures.

claim: The proliferative phenotype observed for lapatinib is likely to necessitate a dynamic, reversible inhibitor binding.
source: This indicates that the proliferative phenotype observed for lapatinib is likely to necessitate a dynamic, reversible inhibitor binding.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the comparison between lapatinib (reversible) and neratinib (irreversible) effects.

claim: Bosutinib strongly binds to HER3.
source: In line with previous observations, we confirmed that HER3 strongly binds bosutinib.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by TSA data in Figure 2a and citations.

claim: Lapatinib was not able to provide a noticeable thermal shift to HER3.
source: Significantly, lapatinib was not able to provide a noticeable thermal shift, which corresponds to previously published results indicating HER3 does not bind lapatinib with high affinity (Davis et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by TSA data and a citation.

claim: Lapatinib conferred strongly increased thermal stability to HER2.
source: While lapatinib was able to confer strongly increased thermal stability to HER2, bosutinib was not (Figure 2b).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by TSA data shown in Figure 2b.

claim: SKBR3 cells treated with bosutinib over 72 hr show a dose dependent induction of proliferation without additional NRG stimulation.
source: In a 2D proliferation assay, SKBR3 cells treated with bosutinib over 72 hr show a dose dependent induction of proliferation without additional NRG stimulation (Figure 2—figure supplement 1b).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by experimental data shown in the referenced figure.

claim: Introduction of the ATP-binding deficient HER3KGG mutant into MCF7 cells shows abrogation of ligand-induced trans-phosphorylation of HER3 by HER2.
source: Introduction of this ATP-binding deficient HER3KGG mutant into MCF7 cells shows abrogation of ligand-induced trans-phosphorylation of HER3 by HER2 (Figure 2d).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 2d.

claim: SKBR3 cells ectopically expressing HER3wt or HER3KGG show a differential proliferative behaviour upon lapatinib ±NRG treatment.
source: SKBR3 cells ectopically expressing HER3wt or HER3KGG show a differential proliferative behaviour upon lapatinib ±NRG treatment.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by experimental data in Figure 2—figure supplement 1f.

claim: Wild type HER3 showed increased thermal stability in cells in the presence of 50 nM bosutinib, while HER3KGG did not.
source: Where wild type HER3 showed increased thermal stability in cells in the presence of 50 nM bosutinib, HER3KGG did not (Figure 2—figure supplement 1g).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by CETSA data shown in the referenced figure.

claim: Ectopic expression of wild type HER3, but not HER3KGG or HER3T787M, enhances bosutinib-mediated proliferation.
source: Ectopic expression of wild type HER3, but not HER3KGG or HER3T787M, enhances bosutinib-mediated proliferation, indicating this behaviour is driven by bosutinib binding to HER3 directly (Figure 2e).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2e.

claim: Nucleotide pocket occupation in HER3 is essential for its ability to sustain a proliferative signalling pathway under distinct circumstances.
source: The HER3KGG and bosutinib results indicate that nucleotide pocket occupation in HER3 is essential for its ability to sustain a proliferative signalling pathway under distinct circumstances: in the acute response to growth factor, in promoting ligand-inhibitor cooperative proliferation and even after treatment with a HER3-binding inhibitor.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental results with HER3KGG and bosutinib.

claim: At endogenous protein levels in SKBR3 cells, lapatinib-driven HER2-HER3 heterodimerisation occurs to levels similar to those seen with NRG.
source: At endogenous protein levels in SKBR3 cells, we observe lapatinib-driven HER2-HER3 heterodimerisation to levels similar to those seen with NRG (Figure 3a).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by FRET-FLIM data shown in Figure 3a.

claim: The lapatinib-induced dimerisation occurs in the absence of exogenously added NRG.
source: Interestingly, the lapatinib-induced dimerisation occurs in the absence of exogenously added NRG, indicating a HER2-HER3 dimer that is driven primarily through intracellular domain interactions.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by FRET-FLIM data in Figure 3.

claim: MCF7 cells expressing low levels of endogenous HER2 and HER3 display lapatinib-induced heterodimerisation of ectopically expressed GFP-HER2wt and HA-HER3wt.
source: MCF7 cells, which express low levels of endogenous HER2 and HER3 compared to SKBR3, also display lapatinib-induced heterodimerisation of ectopically expressed GFP-HER2wt and HA-HER3wt (Figure 3b).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by FRET-FLIM data shown in Figure 3b.

claim: The introduction of the nucleotide pocket compromised HER3KGG mutant strongly disrupts inhibitor-promoted heterodimerisation.
source: This is also reflected in the case of lapatinib-induced heterodimer formation, where the introduction of the nucleotide pocket compromised HER3KGG mutant strongly disrupts inhibitor-promoted heterodimerisation (Figure 3c).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by FRET-FLIM data shown in Figure 3c.

claim: Bosutinib was able to directly promote heterodimerisation between HER2 and HER3.
source: In line with the proliferative effects described above, bosutinib was also able to directly promote heterodimerisation between HER2 and HER3 (Figure 3d).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by FRET-FLIM data shown in Figure 3d.

claim: Treatment with either NRG, lapatinib, or bosutinib showed a shift in cluster population size compared to control, implying the formation of higher-order oligomers rather than dimers.
source: Treatment with either NRG, lapatinib, or bosutinib showed a shift in cluster population size compared to control, implying the formation of higher-order oligomers rather than dimers (Figure 3e,f).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by STORM data shown in Figure 3e,f.

claim: The active signalling dimer in the EGFR family adopts an asymmetric orientation.
source: The active signalling dimer in the EGFR family adopts an asymmetric orientation, in which there is a distinct division of labour in the activator-receiver pairing.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with supporting context from the literature.

claim: For a HER2 α-C helix in the active, 'in' position, lapatinib binding results in a potential steric clash with HER2E770/M774.
source: Our modelling showed that, for a HER2 α-C helix in the active, 'in' position, lapatinib binding results in a potential steric clash with HER2E770/M774 (Figure 4—figure supplement 1a,b).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by molecular modeling shown in the referenced figures.

claim: The I714Q mutation in HER2 disrupted the lapatinib-driven HER2-HER3 association.
source: The I714Q mutation in HER2, which renders the receptor receiver-impaired, disrupted the lapatinib-driven HER2-HER3 association, indicating it is retained in the lapatinib-induced dimer interface (Figure 4b).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by FRET-FLIM data shown in Figure 4b.

claim: The reciprocal activator-impaired mutation in HER3 (HER3V945R) did not disrupt lapatinib-mediated heterodimerisation.
source: However, the reciprocal activator-impaired mutation in HER3 (HER3V945R) did not disrupt lapatinib-mediated heterodimerisation, although it efficiently suppressed the canonical active dimer after ligand-induced heterodimerisation (Figure 4c).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by FRET-FLIM data shown in Figure 4c.

claim: The inhibitor binding is able to robustly induce a heterodimer between HER2 and HER3, which is distinct from the canonical active heterodimer induced after growth factor stimulation.
source: It is surmised that the inhibitor binding is able to robustly induce a heterodimer between HER2 and HER3, which is distinct from the canonical active heterodimer induced after growth factor stimulation.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the mutational analysis and FRET-FLIM data.

claim: HER3 lacks the conserved glutamate residue in the α-C helix.
source: As HER3 lacks the conserved glutamate residue in the α-C helix, HER3K742 is unable to form the salt bridge normally observed in active kinase domain structures (Huse and Kuriyan, 2002).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with a supporting citation.

claim: The HER3 ATP-bound conformation does not show a classical active conformation with the α-C helix tilted inward.
source: The HER3 ATP-bound conformation therefore does not show a classical active conformation with the α-C helix tilted inward (Jura et al., 2009b; Shi et al., 2010), but instead resembles the inactive conformation seen in kinases bound to type II inhibitors such as lapatinib.
evidence: This is stated with supporting citations.

claim: HER2I714 is present in the interaction interface of both the EGFR-like, staggered orientation, as well as in the head-to-head, HER3-like orientation.
source: HER2I714 is present in the interaction interface of both the EGFR-like, staggered orientation, as well as in the head-to-head, HER3-like orientation.
evidence: This is stated based on molecular modeling results.

claim: The HER2N764R/K765F mutant disrupted heterodimerisation upon lapatinib binding.
source: The HER2N764R/K765F mutant disrupted heterodimerisation upon lapatinib binding, whereas HER2I748R/V750R showed no difference in heterodimer formation.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by FRET-FLIM data shown in Figure 5c.

claim: The lapatinib-induced HER2-HER3 heterodimer adopts a symmetrical, head-to-head orientation, similar to the one observed in the HER3 kinase domain crystal lattice.
source: These mutational FRET/FLIM data is consistent with our model that the lapatinib-induced HER2-HER3 heterodimer adopts a symmetrical, head-to-head orientation, similar to the one observed in the HER3 kinase domain crystal lattice (Jura et al., 2009b) (Figure 5b).
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion drawn from mutational analysis and FRET-FLIM data, with a supporting citation.

claim: The HER3V945R active dimer mutant did not disrupt drug-growth factor cooperative proliferation.
source: While the HER3V945R active dimer mutant did not disrupt drug-growth factor cooperative proliferation, the HER3L700F mutant did (Figure 6d–e).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by proliferation assay data shown in Figure 6d-e.

claim: The HER3L700F mutant disrupted drug-growth factor cooperative proliferation.
source: While the HER3V945R active dimer mutant did not disrupt drug-growth factor cooperative proliferation, the HER3L700F mutant did (Figure 6d–e).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by proliferation assay data shown in Figure 6d-e.

claim: The inhibitor-induced heterodimer of HER2 and HER3 is consistent with a head-to-head, symmetrical conformation, and it plays an important role in the synergistic proliferative effects of lapatinib and NRG.
source: Combined, this indicates that the inhibitor-induced heterodimer of HER2 and HER3 is consistent with a head-to-head, symmetrical conformation, and it plays an important role in the synergistic proliferative effects of lapatinib and NRG.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the mutational analysis and proliferation assay data.

claim: This is the first time a functional role has been ascribed to heterodimers consistent with the HER3-like head-to-head interface in cells.
source: Although this conformation has been described from the HER3 kinase domain crystal lattice (Jura et al., 2009b), to our knowledge it is the first time a functional role has been ascribed to heterodimers consistent with this interface in cells.
evidence: This is stated as a novel finding with a supporting citation to the structural work.

claim: The conformational dynamics of HER2-HER3 heterodimerisation are an important consideration for evaluating existing and future targeted therapy intervention strategies against HER2+ breast cancer.
source: The conformational dynamics of HER2-HER3 heterodimerisation are an important consideration for evaluating existing and future targeted therapy intervention strategies against HER2+ breast cancer and other HER family driven cancers.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion in the Discussion section.

claim: Lapatinib itself is able to promote heterodimerisation between the kinase domains of HER2 and HER3, stabilising an orientation consistent with a symmetric, head-to-head kinase domain heterodimer.
source: Lapatinib itself is able to promote heterodimerisation between the kinase domains of HER2 and HER3, stabilising an orientation consistent with a symmetric, head-to-head kinase domain heterodimer that is distinct from the canonical, asymmetric, head-to-tail active kinase domain orientation that occurs throughout the EGFR family.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion in the Discussion section, summarizing the findings.

claim: Sequestering HER2 and HER3 in lapatinib-bound heterodimers was of benefit to NRG-mediated proliferative signalling.
source: Sequestering HER2 and HER3 in these inactive, lapatinib-bound heterodimers was of benefit to NRG-mediated proliferative signalling.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion in the Discussion section.

claim: Lapatinib is likely to induce higher order oligomers.
source: While the FRET-FLIM analysis of the lapatinib-induced dimerisation was not able to differentiate between heterodimers or higher order oligomers, our clustering data shows that lapatinib is likely to induce higher order oligomers.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section and supported by STORM data in Figure 3.

claim: Lapatinib-induced dimers may act as nucleation points for larger oligomeric signalling platforms.
source: Because of the modelled symmetrical nature of these lapatinib-induced dimers, in which both lapatinib-bound HER2 and HER3 would be conformationally available as 'activator' receptors for additional oligomerization partners, it is not inconceivable they may act as nucleation points for larger oligomeric signalling platforms.
evidence: This is stated as speculation in the Discussion section.

claim: The formation of lapatinib-induced oligomeric platforms may facilitate a transition into active signalling heterodimers upon ligand binding.
source: The formation of lapatinib-induced oligomeric platforms may facilitate a transition into active signalling heterodimers upon ligand binding, due to the availability of dimerisation partners in immediate proximity within these drug-induced oligomer platforms.
evidence: This is stated as speculation in the Discussion section.

claim: Both the lapatinib-induced HER2-HER3 heterodimerisation and the downstream lapatinib-NRG synergistic effects on proliferation depended on the ability of HER3 to bind ATP.
source: Both the lapatinib-induced HER2-HER3 heterodimerisation and the downstream lapatinib-NRG synergistic effects on proliferation depended on the ability of HER3 to bind ATP.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion in the Discussion section, summarizing the findings.

claim: HER3 has been shown to retain a measure of autophosphorylation activity (not transphosphorylation) under specific circumstances.
source: Although usually classified as a pseudokinase, HER3 has been shown to retain a measure of autophosphorylation activity (not transphosphorylation) under specific circumstances (Shi et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated with a supporting citation.

claim: Nucleotide binding pocket occupation performs a structural role that is critical to HER3 function, and apparently independent of any retained catalytic activity.
source: We show HER2-HER3 heterodimerisation and downstream proliferative effects can be elicited by the addition of the HER3-binding inhibitor bosutinib, indicating that nucleotide binding pocket occupation performs a structural role that is critical to HER3 function, and apparently independent of any retained catalytic activity.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion in the Discussion section.

claim: Stabilisation of the HER3 kinase domain with an ATP-competitive kinase inhibitor can have a stimulating effect on HER2+ breast cancer cell proliferation.
source: Our data show, however, that stabilisation of the HER3 kinase domain with an ATP-competitive kinase inhibitor can have a stimulating effect on HER2+ breast cancer cell proliferation.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion in the Discussion section.

claim: The development of small molecule targeted therapy against HER3 for use in HER2+ breast cancer needs to be directed away from stabilising the HER3 ATP binding pocket occupied conformer and rather towards stabilising the apo, inactive conformer.
source: This indicates that the development of small molecule targeted therapy against HER3 for use in HER2+ breast cancer needs to be directed away from stabilising the HER3 ATP binding pocket occupied conformer and rather towards stabilising the apo, inactive conformer.
evidence: This is stated as a recommendation in the Discussion section based on the findings.

claim: The substantial effect that lower doses of lapatinib have on proliferation in the presence of growth factor may have an impact on the establishment of lapatinib-resistance in vivo.
source: The substantial effect that lower doses of lapatinib have on proliferation in the presence of growth factor may have an impact on the establishment of lapatinib-resistance in vivo.
evidence: This is stated as speculation in the Discussion section.

claim: Resistance to lapatinib occurs much more readily if lapatinib is administered continuously at low doses than if it's used intermittently at high dose in xenograft models.
source: This is in accordance with the observation from xenograft models that resistance occurs much more readily if lapatinib is administered continuously at low doses than if it's used intermittently at high dose (Amin et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated with a supporting citation.

claim: Increased production of growth factors (including NRG) is a well-described resistance mechanism against HER2-targeted therapy.
source: Increased production of growth factors (including NRG) is a well-described resistance mechanism against HER2-targeted therapy (reviewed in [Claus et al., 2014]).
evidence: This is stated with a supporting citation to a review.

claim: NRG production by the microenvironment has been shown to play a role in metastatic spread of ovarian cancer cells that express high levels of HER3.
source: NRG production by the microenvironment has also been shown to play a role in metastatic spread of ovarian cancer cells that express high levels of HER3 (Pradeep et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated with a supporting citation.

claim: High expression levels of NRG in HER2+ breast cancer patients showed a strong correlation with disease recurrence.
source: High expression levels of NRG in HER2+ breast cancer patients showed a strong correlation with disease recurrence (Xia et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated with a supporting citation.

claim: Several somatic mutations in HER3 observed in cancer fall within the extracellular domain and have a potential effect on ligand-binding affinity.
source: Several somatic mutations in HER3 observed in cancer fall within the extracellular domain and have a potential effect on ligand-binding affinity (Jaiswal et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated with a supporting citation.

claim: The results provide a potential molecular mechanism for the disappointing results observed in a recent Phase III study of lapatinib used in an adjuvant setting (ALTTO trial).
source: Our results provide a potential molecular mechanism for the disappointing results observed in a recent Phase III study of lapatinib used in an adjuvant setting (ALTTO trial) (Piccart-Gebhart et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion in the Discussion section with a supporting citation.

claim: The lapatinib-only arm of the ALTTO trial was terminated prematurely.
source: The lapatinib-only arm of this study was terminated prematurely, and the effects observed in the adjuvant setting for both lapatinib-trastuzumab co-treatment and trastuzumab treatment followed by lapatinib were not significant.
evidence: This is stated with reference to the ALTTO trial.

claim: HER2 has no known ligand.
source: While HER2 itself has no known ligand, HER3 binds the growth factor neuregulin (NRG, also known as heregulin or HRG) to induce heterodimerisation and signalling (Sliwkowski et al., 1994).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge.

claim: HER3 is a pseudokinase.
source: The pseudokinase HER3, heterodimerisation partner of HER2, is widely implicated in the resistance to HER2-mediated therapy.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the abstract.

claim: HER3 is able to bind ATP.
source: HER3 is able to bind ATP (crystallised as PDB ID 3KEX, 3LMG), as well as the Src/ABL inhibitor Bosutinib (PDB ID 4OTW) (Levinson and Boxer, 2014; Davis et al., 2011; Jura et al., 2009b; Murphy et al., 2014; Shi et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated with supporting citations to structural studies.

claim: Lapatinib binds HER3 in vitro with very low affinity (Kd = 5.5 μM).
source: Although HER3 has been shown to bind lapatinib in vitro with very low affinity (Kd = 5.5 μM) (Davis et al., 2011), the synergistic behaviour between lapatinib and NRG occurs in cells at a ~ 50 x lower dose than the in vitro Kd, indicating that any binding of lapatinib to HER3 would likely be minor under these conditions.
evidence: This is stated with a supporting citation.

claim: Transient knockdown of HER3 with two different siRNA oligonucleotides shows a modest, but consistent reduction in the proliferative effect of ligand-inhibitor co-treatment.
source: Moreover, transient knockdown of HER3 with two different siRNA oligonucleotides shows a modest, but consistent reduction in the proliferative effect of ligand-inhibitor co-treatment, implicating HER3 as the relevant growth factor-binding receptor for this NRG response (Figure 1—figure supplement 1j).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by experimental data shown in the referenced figure.

claim: The irreversible inhibitor neratinib binds the same inactive conformation as lapatinib and with similar binding affinity.
source: The irreversible inhibitor neratinib binds the same inactive conformation as lapatinib and with similar binding affinity (Davis et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated with a supporting citation.

claim: Neratinib is an irreversible inhibitor and forms a covalent bond with HER2C805.
source: However, neratinib is an irreversible inhibitor and forms a covalent bond with HER2C805, a residue conserved in EGFR and HER4 but not HER3.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge.

claim: The induction of HER2 and HER3 phosphorylation seen in western blot analysis of lapatinib-NRG co-treated 3D spheroids was absent in neratinib-NRG co-treatment.
source: Similarly, the induction of HER2 and HER3 phosphorylation seen in western blot analysis of lapatinib-NRG co-treated 3D spheroids was absent in neratinib-NRG co-treatment (Figure 1—figure supplement 1l, Figure 1—figure supplement 2d).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Western blot data shown in the referenced figures.

claim: HER3K742 was mutated to methionine to hinder ATP α-phosphate coordination, which by itself has been shown to reduce HER3 mant-ATP binding affinity.
source: HER3K742 was mutated to methionine to hinder ATP α-phosphate coordination, which by itself has been shown to reduce HER3 mant-ATP binding affinity (Shi et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated with a supporting citation.

claim: Both HER3KGG and HER3T787M showed normal localization to the plasma membrane, as measured by flow cytometry.
source: Both HER3KGG and HER3T787M showed normal localization to the plasma membrane, as measured by flow cytometry, indicating that these mutations did not compromise the receptor and its traffic to the plasma membrane (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by flow cytometry data shown in the referenced figure.

claim: The proliferative effects of lapatinib and NRG on SKBR3 cells were also observed in 3D spheroid cultures.
source: The proliferative effects of lapatinib and NRG on SKBR3 cells were also observed in 3D spheroid cultures.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by experimental data in Figure 1c.

claim: In 3D spheroid culture the addition of NRG to lapatinib-treated cells rescues SKBR3 cells from lapatinib-induced cytotoxicity/cytostasis.
source: As seen in 2D culture systems, in 3D spheroid culture the addition of NRG to lapatinib-treated cells rescues SKBR3 cells from lapatinib-induced cytotoxicity/cytostasis (Figure 1c, Figure 1—figure supplement 1k–l).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by experimental data shown in the referenced figures.

claim: Lapatinib and NRG share a cooperative effect on the induction of proliferation in 3D spheroid cultures, where spheroid size is greater for inhibitor-ligand co-treatment conditions than for those treated with growth factor alone.
source: Lapatinib and NRG share a cooperative effect on the induction of proliferation in 3D spheroid cultures, where spheroid size is greater for inhibitor-ligand co-treatment conditions than for those treated with growth factor alone.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by experimental data in Figure 1c.

claim: Bosutinib has been shown to bind strongly to HER3 but not to other EGFR family members.
source: To separate the structural and trace catalytic roles that ATP-binding could fulfill in HER3, we used the ATP-competitive Src/Abl inhibitor bosutinib, which has been shown to bind strongly to HER3 but not to other EGFR family members (Levinson and Boxer, 2014; Davis et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated with supporting citations.

claim: HER2 is not a strong bosutinib binder.
source: This is in line with previously published data that indicates HER2 is not a strong bosutinib binder (Davis et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated with a supporting citation.

claim: The ability of bosutinib to induce SKBR3 cell proliferation appears to be an EGFR-family mediated event, as lapatinib treatment can curtail its effects in a dose-dependent manner.
source: The ability of bosutinib to induce SKBR3 cell proliferation appears to be an EGFR-family mediated event, as lapatinib treatment can curtail its effects in a dose-dependent manner (Figure 2—figure supplement 1e).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by experimental data shown in the referenced figure.

claim: The active kinase domain dimer in the EGFR family is critically affected by the conformation of the juxtamembrane domain (JMD).
source: On the intracellular side, formation of the active kinase domain dimer is critically affected by the conformation of the juxtamembrane domain (JMD) (Jura et al., 2009a; Thiel and Carpenter, 2007).
evidence: This is stated with supporting citations.

claim: The kinase domains associate in an asymmetric dimer, which resembles the CDK/cyclin-like asymmetric dimer interface.
source: The kinase domains associate in an asymmetric dimer, which resembles the CDK/cyclin-like asymmetric dimer interface (Jeffrey et al., 1995; Zhang et al., 2006).
evidence: This is stated with supporting citations.

claim: In the canonical dimer, one kinase (the 'activator') allows the dimerisation partner (the 'receiver') to adopt an active conformation and become catalytically active.
source: In this canonical dimer, one kinase (the 'activator') allows the dimerisation partner (the 'receiver') to adopt an active conformation and become catalytically active.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about EGFR family kinase domain interactions.

claim: There was a lack of active, asymmetrical kinase domain interactions when the receptor was bound to the ATP-competitive inhibitor lapatinib in near-complete receptors using negative stain electron microscopy.
source: Of note in these receptor dimer formations was the lack of active, asymmetrical kinase domain interactions when the receptor was bound to the ATP-competitive inhibitor lapatinib (Mi et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated with a supporting citation.

claim: The conformation of the active kinase domain interaction has been validated for EGFR-HER3 and HER2-HER3.
source: The conformation of the active kinase domain interaction has been validated for EGFR-HER3 and HER2-HER3 (Jura et al., 2009b; Littlefield et al., 2014; van Lengerich et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated with supporting citations.

claim: EGFR-family receptors can form higher order oligomers.
source: A multitude of studies, using a variety of techniques, have confirmed that EGFR-family receptors can form higher order oligomers, and that the exact nature of these oligomers is modulated by a variety of conditions, including receptor density, ligand presence, ligand type and temperature-dependent membrane behaviour (Clayton et al., 2005; Clayton et al., 2007; Huang et al., 2016; Nagy et al., 2010; Needham et al., 2016; Saffarian et al., 2007; van Lengerich et al., 2017; Yang et al., 2007; Zhang et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated with multiple supporting citations.

claim: Occupation of the nucleotide binding pocket with ATP (or an inhibitor) is a major determinant of protein behaviour in PKCε, conferring the structural stability required for protein–protein interactions to occur and priming sites to be stably phosphorylated.
source: We have shown previously that within a kinase, in this case PKCε, occupation of the nucleotide binding pocket with ATP (or an inhibitor) is a major determinant of protein behaviour, conferring the structural stability required for protein–protein interactions to occur and priming sites to be stably phosphorylated (Cameron et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated with a supporting citation.

claim: Similar effects of nucleotide binding pocket occupation have been observed in several additional kinases, including PKB/Akt, IRE1, and AMPK.
